title.narrative: Media Development and Media in Emergency

description.narrative: Free, independent, pluralistic and professionally equipped media institutions are a cornerstone of well-functioning societies, providing the public with the reliable information needed to participate in civic life, hold power to account, and navigate an increasingly complex world. However, media institutions worldwide are under mounting pressure from technological advancements, shrinking revenues, misinformation, and the growing frequency of crises and disasters, all of which demand continuous investment in editorial capacity, operational resilience, and professional standards. Through this work plan, UNESCO will provide strategic guidance and technical support to media institutions across three interconnected areas: broad media development, crisis preparedness and response, and digital innovation, ensuring that institutions of all types, sizes, and contexts can fulfil their public interest mandate, serve their communities under all conditions, and engage with change from a position of active agency.
